You control a robot (**two 6-DoF ALOHA (ViperX) arms with parallel-jaw grippers on a fixed base**) **as if it were real hardware**: the simulator runs in a service you cannot open. You get one
client and one episode. **Task:** Separate and place the entire removable metal ring inside the green dashed goal region. Keep the post, cord, beads and end discs on the puzzle/system side.

## Success requirements

- Put every part of the entire removable metal ring inside the fixed goal volume, leaving at least 1 mm inside its horizontal border. The centre alone is insufficient; no tip, spike, ring segment or cord segment may remain outside.
- Keep the target above the tabletop (contact tolerance 1 mm below the surface) and within the goal volume'"'"'s height. It need not touch the table. The goal volume extends 230.257 mm above the tabletop.
- Keep the post, cord, beads and end discs, and every other remaining puzzle component, entirely on the system side of the fixed separator. Moving the whole puzzle into the goal is not completion.
- Keep each target rigid part'"'"'s linear speed at most 1 mm/s and angular speed at most 0.02 rad/s. Holding the target with the gripper is allowed; release is not required.
- Keep all final conditions satisfied together for at least 0.5 s of simulation time. If any final condition stops holding, the confirmation interval starts again. A brief qualifying pose is not enough; let the simulation advance through the full interval.

## Grader details (in addition to the requirements above)

- Goal square in this instance: the inner edge of the dashed green line is the containment limit (the whole line lies outside it); it encloses a 238.3 mm x 238.3 mm square. Every point counts: for a rigid part every vertex of its visual and collision meshes; for the cord every vertex of its links (capsules).
- The separator is an invisible, fixed vertical plane parallel to the goal square'"'"'s near edge, 5 mm beyond the point of all remaining components that was closest to the goal square at the start; the square'"'"'s near edge is at least 30 mm beyond it. The cord, beads and end discs are free to move (their speed is not checked), but no point of them may cross that plane.
- The cord is a chain of 87 rigid capsule links (14.02 mm long, 7 mm thick) on ball joints that bend and twist freely (no spring), with damping. The links do not deform: nothing about the cord'"'"'s shape or volume ends the episode. A part of the chain (a link, bead, end disc or the ring) moving faster than 3 m/s or spinning faster than 120 rad/s is slowed by extra damping (a speed clamp); this is not reported and does not end the episode.
- Robot safety (this benchmark'"'"'s tooling): no gripper target goes lower than 15 mm below the tabletop; a commanded target that would bring any part of a gripper lower is stopped there, on the commanded path. The fingertips reach about 16 mm beyond the tool frame (TCP) along its approach axis, open or closed. Arm drive torques are capped (the effort limits in robot_spec), so an arm pushing against an obstacle stalls at that torque. An arm with any part more than 5 mm deep in a fixed object (a fixture, the table) is stopped where it is: its joint targets become its measured joints for that control step, so it stops pushing (reported in clipped[]).
- Forcing is recorded, not judged: an arm drive (not a gripper drive) at 95% of its torque cap or more while that arm'"'"'s gripper, or a part it holds, presses on anything else with 20 N or more in total is forcing; 0.5 s of it on every physics tick is a forcing event in the evidence (`meta["safety"]

### Action types

- `joint_position` (14): `left/waist`, `left/shoulder`, `left/elbow`, `left/forearm_roll`, `left/wrist_angle`, `left/wrist_rotate`, `left_native_gripper`, `right/waist`, `right/shoulder`, `right/elbow`, `right/forearm_roll`, `right/wrist_angle`, `right/wrist_rotate`, `right_native_gripper`. arm `left`: 6 joint targets (rad), then `left_native_gripper` = native drive target (m, limits 0.002 .. 0.03 …
Rows are `dt` apart (`1/40 ≤ dt ≤ 0.5` s, a multiple of the control period); a chunk may cover at most 10 s;
out-of-limit values are clipped and listed in `meta["clipped"]` (limits in the spec). The gripper switches at the
row. Use `obs.meta["proprio"]["now"][:14]` as the starting row to move smoothly. An arm joint target moves at most
0.04 rad per control step (1.6 rad/s, the same speed as `ee_pose` rows): a row that asks for more takes
the control steps it needs, and `meta["clipped"]` says so.
The proprio group `gripper_opening` (`res.group("gripper_opening")`) is the measured gap between each gripper'"'"'s finger
pads in metres (0 = the pads touch); the gripper entries of `joint_pos` are in the unit of the gripper command above.

- `ee_pose` (16): per arm (in the order ['"'"'left'"'"', '"'"'right'"'"']) `x y z qw qx qy qz gripper`; world frame (origin at the robot'"'"'s root link on its mounting, +z up; the frame of the proprio TCP pose and the camera extrinsics); quaternions wxyz. Each row is solved by inverse kinematics (no collision checking) and driven to in joint
space; an arm whose IK fails holds and is reported in `meta["plan"]`. The pose is each gripper'"'"'s **tool frame** (TCP;

poses, so an observed pose is a valid target. At most 50 rows per submit. A row whose IK solution lies more than
0.5 rad from the current joints on any joint is refused the same way as a failed IK (for a small pose change that is
another IK branch, which would swing the arm): split long moves into rows a few cm and degrees apart.
- One call returns at most 2000 images (`spec["max_frames_per_call"]`: cameras x frames; a frame with
`depth="frames"` counts 4). A request that would exceed it is answered 400 before anything moves: ask for
fewer cameras, a lower `video_fps` or a shorter call. Rows that take longer than planned (the speed limit, `ee_pose`)
stop adding frames at that number; the motion is executed in full and `meta["frames_skipped"]` counts them.
- Both action types: no gripper target goes lower than 15 mm below the tabletop; a target that would bring any part of
a gripper lower is stopped there and listed in `meta["clipped"]`. Every response'"'"'s `meta["safety"]` reports, since the
previous call, forcing (the arms'"'"' pressing loads and forcing events), the deepest task contact, the longest time above
its sustained limit and the review events (rigid families), the lowest rope / cord volume ratio (soft families) and the
table-guard stops, against the limits above.
